sources: dossier=silent on wait-set-drain-on-park specifically; doc=parked-state.md (pre-fix) omitted any mention of wait-set draining on park; code=lib/runtime/runner_terminal_park.go:89 calls drainWaitSetOnSettled, which calls evaluateGatesAfterDrain -> evaluateOneGate, which calls anySubscribedUpstreamInFlight (lib/runtime/runner_terminal.go:246-310) and gates on cascade.IsInFlight(state) (lib/foundation/cascade/state.go:163-168, NodeStateParked included, no held-style co-member exception); design-corpus=wait-set.md:43 independently states the gate evaluator's pending->stale predicate requires 'no subscribed upstream ... has an in-flight run in the same frame (in-flight = state in {pending, stale, running, held, parked})'
note: Traced the actual code path: drainWaitSetOnSettled does mark wait-set rows drained and re-invoke gate evaluation, but evaluateOneGate's separate anySubscribedUpstreamInFlight check unconditionally treats a parked sender as in-flight (no co-member exception, unlike held) and blocks the transition. So a downstream receiver subscribed to the very node that just parked stays gated, not un-gated, while parked -- corroborated independently by wait-set.md's own invariant. The finding's factual claim ('un-gating downstream while the node is parked') does not hold as stated; the drain call is real but functionally inert for the scenario described (it serves sibling-pending reevaluation/bookkeeping, not un-gating a parked sender's own subscribers). Doc's silence on this point is not a defect.
